paras: The attempted lynching of Henry Wade was a failed attempt in August 1895 to lynch a Black man held for the shooting death of Henry Hightower, a young white man, at Martindale, Texas. Wade escaped by running to officers for protection and was afterwards held in jail at Seguin. The episode was reported in two short dispatches from Luling in the Fort Worth Gazette.

On Saturday evening, August 10, Wade had a "difficulty" with Hightower's brother-in-law and struck him on the head with a rock, badly injuring him, according to the Luling correspondent. The next evening Hightower met Wade near the Baptist church at the edge of Martindale, eighteen miles west of Luling, and fired on him twice with a pistol. Wade answered with a shotgun and killed Hightower instantly, and he was then captured and carried to jail at Lockhart.

A second dispatch, dated August 15, said it had been "learned" at Luling that an attempt had been made to lynch Wade. The attempt was "frustrated" when Wade made "a race for the officers" and placed himself under their protection. The dispatch gave no date or place for the attempt and did not identify or count the would-be lynchers.
Wade was reported in jail at Seguin rather than Lockhart, though neither dispatch says when or why he was moved. No report of an inquest, indictment or trial appears in the coverage.

The Fort Worth Gazette ran the shooting on August 14 under the headline "Killed by a Negro." even though its own account had Hightower firing first. Three days later it ran the lynching attempt as "A Lynching Frustrated.", a three-sentence item that referred to Wade only as "the negro" after first naming him and made no comment on the attackers. No other paper, white or Black, was found carrying either story.

The first dispatch placed Wade in the Lockhart jail after his capture, while the second implies he was outside a jail when the lynching attempt came, since he escaped by running to officers. Neither report reconciles the two accounts.

bases: A2 reports an attempt to lynch Henry Wade that failed when he placed himself under officers' protection; no one was killed (A2).

Wade survived: the attempt to lynch him was 'frustrated' and he was jailed at Seguin (A2); the attempt was over his killing of Henry Hightower (A1, A2), but the report names no attackers and gives no number.
The lynching attempt appears only in one Luling dispatch to the Fort Worth Gazette (A2); the earlier report of the shooting (A1) is from the same paper and correspondent and does not mention it.

accounts.label: Luling correspondent, first report
accounts.gist: After Wade struck Hightower's brother-in-law with a rock, Hightower met Wade near the Baptist church and fired twice; Wade replied with a shotgun and killed him, and was captured and jailed at Lockhart.

accounts.label: Luling correspondent, second report
accounts.gist: It was 'learned' at Luling that an attempt to lynch Wade had failed because he ran to officers for protection; he was then in jail at Seguin.

framing.detail: The Fort Worth Gazette headlined the shooting 'Killed by a Negro.' while reporting that Hightower fired first, and the lynching attempt 'A Lynching Frustrated.' without comment on the would-be lynchers.

conflicts.note: Probably sequential (Lockhart after capture, Seguin after the lynching attempt), but no report says Wade was moved or why.
